hero.headline: A new dental CAD for the practice and the lab.
hero.subhead: DentalCraft is an application for digital dentistry that you install on your practice or lab computer. It starts with clear aligner planning; more areas of work are planned for later.
hero.microcopy: Early stage. Linux and Windows first. Made in Italy.

presentation.label: Presentation
presentation.headline: What DentalCraft is, and where it stands
presentation.body.1: DentalCraft is a dental CAD. It grows out of an orthodontic aligner planning tool that its author built earlier. It takes up that work and turns it into a dedicated, faster, standalone application, organised like the professional dental CAD suites: a common base and, on top of it, one area for each type of work.
presentation.body.2: The project is at an early stage. Today the application structure, the single file for each case and the 3D view exist. Scan import and the clinical functions are being brought over from the earlier tool and validated.

vision.label: Vision
vision.banner: What follows is intent, not a description of finished features.
vision.headline: Why a new dental CAD
vision.body: Digital planning means long hours on heavy scans and 3D models. We think the tool should stay fast, stay on your computer and stay under the clinician's control. DentalCraft is being built around those ideas.
vision.p1.title: Smooth even with heavy scans.
vision.p1.body: The aim: work on the 3D model without freezes, even with large scans.
vision.p2.title: Not tied to a connection.
vision.p2.body: Cases stay on your computer. You should not need the internet to work.
vision.p3.title: One file for each case.
vision.p3.body: The whole case in a single open, documented file, with an integrity check.
vision.p4.title: Pseudonymised patient data.
vision.p4.body: Case files are designed to carry no patient names.
vision.p5.title: In English and Italian.
vision.p6.title: Linux and Windows first.
vision.p7.title: Built with a regulatory mindset.
vision.p7.body: Requirements, risk management and traceability are carried over from day one.
vision.p8.title: Independent and made in Italy.
vision.microcopy: These are design intentions. They describe where we are heading.
roadmap.label: What's next
roadmap.headline: One application, several areas of work
roadmap.body: DentalCraft will have a common base and, on top of it, one area for each type of work. Aligners comes first. The others are planned, with no dates.
roadmap.alt: Row of five tabs: Aligners in development, then Model Builder, Splint, Crown and Bridge, Implant as planned.

aligners.label: Aligners
aligners.headline: From scan to aligner, in one workspace
aligners.body: The Aligners area is designed to follow the clinical path from intraoral scan to files for printing. The stages below are grouped like the application menu.
aligners.banner: Intended workflow. Each stage is tagged Planned or In progress. Nothing here is finished yet.
aligners.s2.micro: Get the scans ready for planning.
aligners.s2.stages: Orientation and arch; FDI tooth numbering; tooth segmentation; tooth and gingiva reconstruction
aligners.s3.stages: Space analysis; Little irregularity index; Bolton analysis
aligners.s4.micro: Define the target and the steps.
aligners.s4.stages: Setup of the final position; staging per aligner with movement limits for each tooth; interproximal reduction (IPR); attachments
aligners.s5.stages: Occlusion and bite, including bite with aligners
aligners.s6.stages: Aligner shell with thickness and clearance; trim line; identification stamp; print check
aligners.s8.stages: STL export for each stage; reports

technology.label: In practice
technology.headline: Your work, your data
technology.body: Choices made for speed, control and traceability of the work.
technology.i1.title: An application on your computer.
technology.i1.body: You install and use it on the practice or lab computer, not through a browser.
technology.i2.title: A smooth 3D view.
technology.i2.body: Designed to handle even the most detailed scans smoothly.
technology.i3.title: One file for each case.
technology.i3.body: An open, documented file with an integrity check.
technology.i4.title: Privacy by design.
technology.i4.body: Patient data is pseudonymised: no names in case files.
technology.i5.title: Cases stay with you.
technology.i5.body: You work on cases saved on your computer. An account is planned for licences and support only.
technology.i6.title: Two languages.
technology.microcopy: Details will be published once the file format is final.
regulatory.label: Regulatory
regulatory.headline: Honest about where we are
regulatory.callout: In development. Not a medical device. Not for clinical use.
regulatory.body.1: DentalCraft is not a medical device and is not certified. It must not be used for clinical purposes.
regulatory.body.2: The project is being built with a regulatory mindset: requirements, risk management and traceability are taken over from the earlier work. The intention is to pursue the appropriate medical-device conformity path when the software is ready for it. That is an intention, not a status.
faq.label: FAQ
faq.headline: Questions, answered plainly
faq.a1: An alpha version for Linux and Windows can be downloaded from the home page, free of charge, for non-clinical use (evaluation, training, research and design trials). It is in early development: it is not a medical device and not for clinical use. The application structure, the single file for each case and the 3D view exist. Scan import and the clinical functions are being brought over from the earlier tool and validated.
faq.q2: Is it certified? Is it a medical device?
faq.a2: No. DentalCraft is not a medical device and holds no certification. It is not for clinical use. We are building with a regulatory mindset and intend to pursue the appropriate conformity path in the future.
faq.q3: Which computers will it run on?
faq.a3: Linux and Windows first. macOS later.
faq.a5: Cases are designed to stay on your computer. Case files are pseudonymised and carry no patient names. An account is planned only for licences and support.
faq.a6: Yes. An alpha version for Linux and Windows can be downloaded from the home page, free of charge, for non-clinical use: evaluation, training, research and design trials. It is provided as is. It is not a medical device and not for clinical use.
faq.a7: The first area is Aligners, for clear aligner planning. The intended workflow is described on the home page: its stages are in progress or planned, and none is finished yet.
faq.q8: Which files will I be able to use?
faq.a8: The plan is to import scans in STL, OBJ and PLY and to export each stage as STL. Each case is saved in a single open file.
contact.label: Contact
privacy.label: Privacy
privacy.headline: No cookies, no tracking, no forms
privacy.body.1: This website sets no cookies, runs no analytics or tracking scripts, loads nothing from third parties and has no forms. We do not collect personal data through it. Your language choice is kept only in your own browser, so that the site can open in your language next time.
privacy.body.2: Like any website, this one may keep standard access logs (IP address, time, page requested) for security and troubleshooting. If you write to hello@dentalcraft.app, we use your message only to reply.
